title: The interview: does it ask in plain language, and does the plan come back in your words?
observable: An operator-driven dispatch COMPLETES without a technical question being asked of you. Quoted from CODER_DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md capability 2.
why: This has never once been finished. The interview has been opened twice and approved zero times, so everything after the plan card — whether your photos get used, whether the exams grade your actual request, whether the report tells the truth — has never run on a real job. The flags being switched on is not the same as the thing working, and only you can close that gap.

steps.expect: the chat screen, with your name at the top and a box at the bottom that says "Message BlarAI…"
steps.note: If the box is missing or the app is blank, the assistant is not running — stop here and say so. That is a real finding, not something to work around.

steps.target: the "Message BlarAI…" box, then press Enter
steps.text: /dispatch advanced pottery-studio | I run a small pottery studio and I want a proper little website for it, not just one page. A home page, a page listing the pieces I have for sale, a separate page for each piece, and a contact page where someone can send me an enquiry.
steps.expect: it starts ASKING YOU QUESTIONS, one at a time, in ordinary English — about what the site is for, who it is for, what it should feel like. It should NOT ask you anything technical, and it should NOT jump straight to a plan.
steps.note: The word "advanced" is what triggers the interview. Without it you get the short path and this exercise proves nothing.

steps.expect: plain language a non-technical person can answer. If ANY question uses jargon you would not use yourself — framework, endpoint, schema, deploy — that is a failure worth reporting word for word.

steps.target: the message box, as your answer to any one question
steps.expect: it accepts that and moves on, and later tells you it decided that one for you. It must NOT get stuck, repeat the question, or scold you.
steps.note: Being allowed to say "I don't know" is a designed behaviour, not a loophole. If it refuses the answer, that is the finding.

steps.target: the plan card it shows you at the end
steps.expect: YOUR OWN WORDS played back — the phrases you actually typed, not a rewritten version. It should also list anything it assumed on your behalf.

steps.target: the "Approve & build" button on the plan card
steps.expect: it accepts the approval and begins building. This is the step that has never been taken — everything past this point is unproven, so whatever happens next is worth reporting exactly as you see it.
steps.note: The build itself takes hours. You do not wait for it. Stop here; the result appears in tomorrow's report.

cannot_check: Whether the finished website is any good — the build runs for hours after you approve, and its result is graded separately.

Whether your own photos get used. That half of the system has never run either, and the interview does NOT yet ask you for files; you would have to know to put them in the project's assets folder yourself.
How it looks. Appearance is judged by eye and is never auto-passed — it is reported as unverified rather than claimed as working.
rollback: Open the AI Control Panel and press [8] Undo AI changes in a project — that reverses anything the build wrote. If the assistant itself is misbehaving, [S] stops it and [K] stops everything. Turning the interview OFF is a config change rather than a button, so say the word and it is a one-line change on my side.
